title: Realization of Air-Stable Two-Dimensional Superconductor Nb2Pd3Te5 With Quasi-One-Dimensional Pair Density Modulation
authors: Jiayi Wang, Hui Guo, Hao Zhang, Haowei Chen, Peixuan Li, Xianghe Han, Ziang Wang, Siyu Xu, Qian Fang, Haohao Xu, Shixuan Du, Chengmin Shen, Hui Chen, Wang Yao, Hong-Jun Gao
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) superconductors provide a fertile platform for exploring reduced-dimensional superconductivity and emergent quantum phenomena. Incorporating quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) structural motifs into 2D superconductors offers a powerful route to engineer strong electronic anisotropy, enabling unconventional superconducting states and anisotropic superconducting transport functionalities. However, such systems remain rarely realized. Here we report the realization of a 2D superconductor Nb2Pd3Te5, exhibiting an intrinsic quasi-1D pair density modulation. Monolayer and bilayer Nb2Pd3Te5 is synthesized via van-der-Waals epitaxy. Using ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy, we observe the quasi-1D crystal structure and superconductivity below ~0.6 K with a pronounced quasi-1D pair density modulation. Remarkably, both monolayer and bilayer Nb2Pd3Te5 show strong air stability. Our findings establish atomically 2D Nb2Pd3Te5 as a robust and promising platform for exploring novel low-dimensional quantum phenomena and anisotropy-enabled superconducting devices.
summary: This work reports the synthesis and characterization of $	ext{Nb}_2	ext{Pd}_3	ext{Te}_5$, a novel 2D superconductor exhibiting an intrinsic quasi-1D structure. Using advanced STM/STS, the authors confirmed a pronounced quasi-1D modulation in the superconducting pair density and demonstrated the material's remarkable air stability. This establishes the compound as a promising platform for engineering anisotropic superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: The primary goal was to realize and characterize an air-stable, atomically 2D superconductor exhibiting intrinsic quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) pair density modulation.
main_result: The authors successfully synthesized and characterized $	ext{Nb}_2	ext{Pd}_3	ext{Te}_5$ as a robust 2D superconductor showing clear evidence of quasi-1D pair density modulation in its superconducting gap, alongside exceptional air stability.
method: The study employed van-der-Waals epitaxy for synthesis, followed by ultra-low-temperature Scanning Tunneling Microscopy/Spectroscopy (STM/STS) and Raman spectroscopy for characterization.
model_or_system: The physical system is the 2D superconductor $	ext{Nb}_2	ext{Pd}_3	ext{Te}_5$, which possesses an intrinsic quasi-1D crystal structure composed of alternating T- and H-chains. The investigation focuses on the superconducting and electronic properties within this low-dimensional platform.
key_observables: Superconducting gap ($\Delta \sim 121 \mu	ext{eV}$), quasi-1D pair density modulation in $	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$ spectra, ambient stability (structural and chemical), and the intrinsic T-chain/H-chain electronic anisotropy.
important_parameters: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c \approx 613 	ext{ mK}$), operating temperatures ($\sim 5 	ext{ mK}$), and the periodicity of the modulation ($\sim 1.87 	ext{ nm}$).
main_assumptions: The observed modulation is attributed to the intrinsic lattice arrangement of T- and H-chains, rather than necessarily implying long-range Charge Density Wave (CDW) order, which was not confirmed by LEED.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure (T/H-chains), STM topography showing stripe modulation, STS linecuts revealing the quasi-1D modulation of the superconducting gap, and Raman spectra confirming ambient stability.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the synthesis and quasi-1D structure via STM/LEED, then detailing the superconducting properties and the pair density modulation using low-temperature STS, and finally emphasizing the exceptional ambient stability of the material for device applications.
why_interesting: The demonstration of intrinsic quasi-1D electronic and superconducting modulation in a highly stable 2D material provides a clean, tunable platform for studying low-dimensional quantum phenomena, which is highly relevant to superconducting quantum circuits and correlated electron physics.
